podcast.title: "How Time Flies" Broadway Adaptation
podcast.body: Following the successful tour of "How Time Flies," Shatner was so pleased that he decided to take the production to Broadway. After negotiations, the show did make it to Broadway, though with a rejigged format. "When the two are wrapped up, the shot was so pleased that he declared we're taking this thing to Broadway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stop Me If You've Heard This One Before

podcast.title: "How Time Flies" Stage Production (2000s)
podcast.body: Shatner conceived a stage production based on reminiscences from his 60-year career in show business. The show was structured as a celebrity interview in front of an audience, incorporating audio and video clips over 90 minutes with a 15-minute intermission, and toured through Vancouver, Regina, Edmonton, Winnipeg, Toronto, and Montreal. "The tour for the production, which was called How Time Flies, by the way, started in Vancouver and made its way through Regina Edmonton Winnipeg, Toronto Montreal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "The Hockey Song" Sing-along Attempt
podcast.body: Shatner wanted to end each "How Time Flies" show with a sing-along and considered performing "The Hockey Song" by Stompin' Tom Connors. However, he struggled with it in rehearsals, indicating he couldn't quite make it work. "But in rehearsals, he just couldn't seem to make it work."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Documentary Filmmaker
podcast.body: William Shatner is mentioned as another individual who has "turned into documentaries," working with Zach Wilde and others. This comes up in a discussion about Dave Grohl's filmmaking endeavors, suggesting a shared interest in the medium. "Another guy who is turned into documentaries. Who's that William Shatter? Wow. Yeah. There you go."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Style and Philosophy
podcast.body: William Shatner's singing style is described as eccentric, yet he expresses a deep love for music, stating "music is in his soul." He acknowledges that his skills lie in words rather than music, viewing music itself as a "mysterious place to go" even for seasoned musicians. "I am a dearth of that and totally recognize it. So my skills are in words and not music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Philosophy of Experimentation and Failure
podcast.body: Shatner advocates for continuous experimentation in all aspects of life, asserting that "every time should be a time of experimentation," rather than limiting it to specific periods. He firmly believes that failure is a necessary prerequisite for success, as one learns what doesn't work before discovering what does, and that people should be given allowance for this process. "Well, every time should be a time of experimentation. Okay. I should take one year to experiment, not another year. Everything should be filled with experimentation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Private Jet Travel
podcast.body: Shatner travelled between gigs on his private jet during the "How Time Flies" tour, offering a ride from Toronto to Montreal on one occasion. "But when it came time to get from Toronto to Montreal, he invited me on his private jet, which let me tell you something, has ruined me for any air travel for the rest of my life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stop Me If You've Heard This One Before

podcast.title: Regina Brewpub Beer Order
podcast.body: During the "How Time Flies" tour, Shatner was at a brewpub in Regina and, being a beer lover, ordered a flight of various beers. Upon noticing a non-drinker, he gave a direct order to drink beer, using a voice reminiscent of his "Wrath of Khan" character. "Then in a voice right out of the wrath of Khan, he gave me an order. You will drink beer!"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Diverse Post-Ben Folds Five Career
xref.body: Since his time with Ben Folds Five, Ben Folds has pursued a highly varied career, releasing solo albums, collaborating with diverse artists like William Shatner and "Weird Al" Yankovic, composing Hollywood film soundtracks, acting, judging an NBC talent show, serving as an artistic director for a symphony orchestra, hosting a podcast, and writing a memoir. This extensive range of activities demonstrates his versatile talents. "Since then, Ben Foltz has released a number of albums on his own, collaborated with everyone from William Shatton or to Weird Al, written soundtracks for Hollywood films, Dunsome Acting, appeared as a judge on an NBC talent show, served as an artistic director to a symphony orchestra, hosted a podcast and written a memoir."
